answer_1.quote: Human-quality text has long been a holy grail for the output of natural language generation (NLG) systems, serving as an upper bound on their performance.
answer_1.outputs: generated stories, news articles, and recipes

answer_4.quote: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) to collect the text evaluations with non-expert evaluators, commonly used in NLG evaluations (van der Lee et al., 2019).
answer_4.guideline: We asked them to rate the text on a 4-point scale: 1. Definitely human-written 2. Possibly human-written 3. Possibly machine-generated 4. Definitely machine-generated. If they selected option 1, we asked them: 'Why did you select this rating?' Otherwise, they were asked, 'What would you change to make it seem more human-like?'
